why.A: Parallel synchronous calls finish sooner, but the job has no deadline before morning, and per-token cost stays the same, so speed buys nothing here.
why.C: max_tokens only caps output length. It doesn't make per-token pricing cheaper, and it risks cutting reports short.
why.D: Downsizing the model regardless of quality trades away the result itself. The requirement is lower cost for the same work, not worse work.

DVO-01.whenRight: If the report were needed within minutes (an interactive or blocking use), synchronous calls (A) would be right, possibly with a smaller model chosen for quality and latency, not 'regardless of quality'.
DVO-01.trap: "non-urgent … not needed until the following morning" + "cost is the primary concern": latency-tolerant bulk work points to the Message Batches API.

why.A: Temperature controls sampling randomness, not whether the model obeys injected instructions.
why.C: Asking users politely isn't an enforceable control. Attackers ignore it, and the hidden text isn't written by the user anyway.
why.D: A model that follows instructions more readily can be easier to steer with injected instructions. Model size isn't a security boundary.

DVO-02.whenRight: None of the others becomes a primary defence. A stronger model and clear system-prompt instructions can be extra layers, but only on top of isolating untrusted content and least-privilege guardrails.
DVO-02.trap: "hidden text instructing the model" in user-submitted pages: treat retrieved content as untrusted data and enforce controls outside the prompt.

why.A: Logic in system prompts isn't executable, can't reach the live service, and would have to be copied into every application.
why.C: Pasting data gives a stale snapshot, wastes context on every request, and can't perform operations.
why.D: Built-in tools don't reach arbitrary internal APIs. You need a custom tool or an MCP server that wraps the service.

DVO-03.whenRight: If only one application needed the inventory service and reuse didn't matter, a custom tool (function calling) inside that app would be simpler than running an MCP server.
DVO-03.trap: "reusable across several Claude applications and maintained independently": a shared MCP server.
